哥倫比亞三弦琴的共鳴箱常見以胡桃木或雪松製作，琴頸通常為雪松；品絲傳統用紅銅或黃: The soundbox of the tiple colombiano is commonly made of walnut or cedar and the neck usually of cedar; the frets were traditionally copper or brass, and modern instruments more often use brass or steel. The twelve strings are metal: the first course of three is all steel, and the other three courses commonly have a copper centre string with steel strings on either side, the centre string an octave below the outer ones. Outside Colombia the so-called copper strings are often replaced with standard brass- or bronze-wound steel guitar strings. The tuning pegs were wooden at first and later metal-geared; the source does not state the materials of the other parts.
哥倫比亞三弦琴起源文獻零散，最早記載見一八四九年何塞·凱塞多·羅哈斯文章，稱其與: The documentary record of the tiple colombiano's origins is scattered. The earliest mention is an 1849 article by José Caicedo Rojas, which says that it and the bandola were copied from the Spanish vihuela. A Jesuit phrase book of 1680 refers to guitars and tiples being sold in Topaga, but where it originated is unsettled; it is mostly thought to be connected with the Spanish guitar and with the timple of the Canary Islands. The eight-string type of the later nineteenth century is the forerunner of today's twelve-string type, as teaching books of 1868 and 1877 show; makers added strings in the early twentieth century, a document of 1915 mentions twelve strings, a photograph of 1921 shows the present form, and metal-geared machine heads were finally adopted.
哥倫比亞三弦琴音色清亮透徹，具有南美民族樂器典型的明快特質。其音域偏高，音色介於: The tiple colombiano has a clear, transparent timbre with the bright quality typical of South American folk instruments. Its range lies high, its timbre between the guitar and the mandolin, warm yet still clear. The instrument uses courses of two or three strings, which gives a rich resonance and makes a single note sound layered. When plucked the tone is bright and carries well, and it blends well into an ensemble. Compared with the depth and weight of the classical guitar, the tiple is lighter and more nimble; compared with the sharp brightness of the mandolin it has more warmth. The design of the resonator lets notes stay clearly defined while producing handsome overtones, and it suits the heat and cheerfulness of Latin American folk music.
哥倫比亞三弦琴（Tiple Colombiano）為撥弦樂器，屬吉他家族，常見於: The tiple colombiano is a plucked instrument of the guitar family, common in Colombia and regarded as one of its national instruments. It is about three quarters the size of a classical guitar and has twelve strings in four courses of three; the scale length is about 530 mm and the neck usually joins the body at the twelfth fret. It can play the lead or accompany the guitar. In the Hornbostel–Sachs classification it is 321.322-5.
